thread:
Priya: Quick follow-up from last night's outage — want to land a super-light action tracking template + an IC rotation plan so followups don't stall.
Sam: +1. can we keep it tiny? most of our stuff dies in followups because it's too heavy.
Chris: Agree. also we should tag actions with whether they block customer-facing features or are internal.
Priya: Proposed minimal fields: Action, Owner, Priority (P0/P1/P2), Due, Verification criteria, Blockers. Cadence: 48h quick check, then weekly pulse until closed.
Tess: And comms: short 24h status (what's done, who's blocked), +72h summary in #incidents and a short note in the customer-facing incident doc if external.
Priya: Here's a copy-paste template we can use in followups (also for the postmortem action table):
```
Action: Describe the remediation in one line
Owner: full name (pager on-call if applicable)
Priority: P0/P1/P2
Due: YYYY-MM-DD (or "TBD")
Verification: how we'll validate (link to runbook or test)
Blockers: short note if any
Release/Deploy: what release contains the fix (if relevant)
Cost/Impact: rough p99/latency/cost impact to help prioritize
```
Sam: can we add "Rollback criteria"? sometimes fixes need clear rollback thresholds. :thinking_face:
Priya: Good call — add a "Rollback" line (optional).
Chris: For ownership lifecycle: require "owner ack" within 24h of action creation, and a weekly owner pulse until the action is Closed. Automate reminders.
Jordan: I can own the IC rotation calendar and OpsBot reminders. Propose 2-week IC rotation with a 30m handoff doc slot (IC checklist: active incidents, ongoing remediations, exec comms points).
Tess: Handovers should be 10 bullet points max — what is critical, who to call, where the logs/dashboards live.
Priya: For recurring incident patterns: in the 1st follow-up meeting run a 5-min "recurrence triage" — if we see the same symptom twice in 30 days, flag it to "recurring-incidents" board and assign a small investigation spike.
Sam: We should surface recurring flags in the incident list UI and the weekly SRE/infra review.
Chris: Also add a tag for "cost-regression" (token/CPU spend) — Tess's point about cost/latency impact helps prioritize low-effort high-impact fixes.
Jordan: I'll wire OpsBot to create the JIRA ticket when someone pastes the template and marks Owner: — it will fill project=INCIDENTS, label=incident-<id>, and ping owner.
Priya: Next steps: Jordan sets rotation calendar + OpsBot reminders; Sam drafts a one-page timeline template for incident writeups (timeline, actions, root cause, mitigations) and posts by EOD; I'll schedule a 30min review Friday 10:00 to validate owners.
Tess: I'll add the verification metric suggestions to the template (what to measure).
Sam: I'll include an example timeline snippet (events + latency/cost at each step) so people know the expected granularity.
Chris: small note — prefer "owner" to be a person not a team; if team-owned, we need explicit on-call person.
Priya: Agreed. if owner is a team, require a nominated point person.
Jordan: OpsBot: reminder scheduled to post "create jira tasks from followup template" in 24h.
OpsBot: Reminder set — will post in #incidents in 24h and DM owners automatically.
Tess: :thumbsup: thanks everyone, this feels actionable and lightweight.
Priya: Thanks — will capture decisions in the followup doc and link into the postmortem.
